title: Dispatch CUS 3: Two Maps Now Fit the North Ward
summary: Surveyors find several doors where the rejected street plan crosses existing homes.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: Seven doorways have appeared along the routes of Fenwick Lane and Vesper Row. Each opens between a present building and an inhabited address listed in the disputed census. Residents on both sides say the new opening leads into a part of their own house that was formerly a wall.

Mr. Reed has compared both street plans. Alderwick’s existing north ward was built after the council rejected the 1887 proposal. The people behind the new doors say their town approved it. They possess tax receipts, family photographs, and a street directory printed with businesses that have operated for decades.

A woman from Fenwick Lane showed our reporter a photograph of a civic parade through Vesper Row. Its clock tower matches Alderwick’s, but the buildings around it are different. The newspaper in one marcher’s hand bears the familiar title The Alderwick Chronicle. Its masthead names an editor unknown to this office.

Dr. Saye calls the houses a second, coherent arrangement of Alderwick rather than a hallucination produced by the census sheets. She cannot yet say whether the entries brought the streets into contact or merely revealed a boundary already weakening.

The greatest concern is physical. Where two walls meet at a new doorway, both claim the same ground. A pantry floor on Fenwick Lane sank an inch yesterday when a cellar shelf on this side was moved. Surveyors have marked the shared areas and warned residents against altering either building.
